questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Taiwan because it have read about the history of the country and wanted to learn more about it though attending courses at a local university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: NTU is an amazing campus to stay at. The campus is very beautiful, there are many delicious and cheap food, coffee and snack options, many great libraries and study spaces to read in peace and quiet and there are many social activities going on at the campus. However, there can sometimes be a language barrier that can make it hard to understand where you can find help or the social activities you are looking for. But you can always contact the OIA, they are always very friendly and willing to help you further. Taiwan is really a beautiful and amazing country and it has been a privilege to be able to stay here and to learn more about its culture and history.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy most of the time. However, information about the courses beforehand is quite hard to find. It is not sure that the course you are interested in will be set up in your semester, and sometimes there are not information in english - even about the courses taught in english. Also, it takes a bit getting used to, to understand the course system. I used youtube and google a lot to help me understand how I could find information about the courses I wanted to enroll in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Every exchange student is assigned a student volunteer. However, I never met them and only had a short mail-exchange with them, when I asked for help about getting a local phone number, and they gave me a few tips with this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the amount of information upon arrival was good. We were invited to a big information meeting in a student lecture hall, where all the details were explained and contacts were provided.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my room though a Facebook page (I mainly used these two groups: "Short-term apartment in Taipei" and "Rooms & Apartments - Taipei, Taiwan"). It was quite easy, and there were a lot of posts - especially in november/december.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I will recommend you start looking for housing early, if you want to live off campus. It will give you more peace later, when the semester start is getting closer. There are many posts on the facebook groups ("Short-term apartment in Taipei" and "Rooms & Apartments - Taipei, Taiwan") and webpages provided by NTU, where you can look for housing off campus. This is obviously always a risk - so be aware of scams! This ofc applies to everywhere - the difference here is the language barrier.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to submit a few documents, pay an internet bill at a convenience store and obtain a health check to enroll at NTU. I got the health check on a hospital upon arrival in Taiwan, because I did not have enough time to get an x-ray in Denmark. I went to get the health check at Taipei City Hospital Renai Branch, but I would recommend getting it done when you are in Denmark. Then you dont have to stress about it when you arrive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of information was provided, so the registration process was quite straight forward.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
The course registrations process is quite confusing and it takes some time to get used to how you find the information. There are several pages, that provide information about the courses - you can look up:
https://course.ntu.edu.tw/en
. I found this webpage to be useful and more easy to navigate when searching for information about the courses. However, this is not the actual registration page, only used for information. Here you can also filter the courses that are taught in english language.
I was successfull in registering for all the courses I wanted - but not at fist. In the first "round" i was only accepted into two of the courses I wanted, but the system allows you to register if you go to the first class in person. You can then ask the professor for a registration-number and they will give it to you, if there are still room in the course. So I actually ended up with getting all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read about the registration process online, beforehand. Because the information is submitted quite late in the process of registration. But dont stress about getting all the courses you want at first. Usually you will get a second - and a third chance also!:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses I had were very interesting and relevant. However, there were not an overwhelming amount of english-taught courses to choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were quite fitting. Mostly it was the workload that was tough, and not the level. The workload were often very heavy to each of the courses - requiring reading a lot of material, oral presentations quite often and also weekly written response papers in most of the classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at NTU is more focused on learning things by heart in stead of discussing the material. This were reflected in the multiple choice exams, which I found to be not the best way to learn about some material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recommend all of the courses I took. They were all very informative and had very engaged and friendly professors.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Restaurants are quite cheap, while buying groceries can be quite expensive (similar prices to Denmark often)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any clubs at the campus. But I wish I did!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a big student gym, running field and swimming pool at the campus. I did not use any of these, but many of my friends were using them several times a week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going hiking, night markets, restaurants and cafes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going hiking around Taipei (there are many amazing trails around Taipei - do it before it becomes 35+ degrees and 80% humidity though), going to trips to smaller cities in the north and south. Visit Kaohsiung and Tainan. Visit the islands (xiao liuqiu is very pretty). Go to night markets and experience street food snacks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the clubs at the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People go out to eat at restaurants with their friends a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the resources, delicious food and beautiful scenery around NTU campus, dont stress too much about getting the right courses at first - you can usually fix this later (I got all the courses I wanted in the end), participate in the social life around campus (I wish I did this more!).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NTU is quite bureaucratic in its system - but nothing too hard or difficult about it - it can just feel a bit heavy sometimes. But people are very helpful so you can always get help on how to navigate all the documents and requirements that are needed for registration and course selection!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know more about the history and culture of Taiwan - it is really an amazing country! I will recommend anyone to visit, and going there for a few months has been a huge experience and privilege I will never forget!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier can be quite tough sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
